title: Hybrid PACS | On-Premise Node Plus Cloud Layer | AuraPACS
meta: Hybrid PACS explained: which parts of AuraPACS run on the node in your centre, which run in the cloud, and exactly what keeps working when power or internet fails.
h1: Hybrid PACS: local where it must be fast, cloud where it must be reachable.
pill: Built for Indian power and connectivity
sub: A hybrid PACS splits the work in two. An on-premise node inside the centre receives, stores and serves studies over the local network. A thin cloud layer adds remote reading, WhatsApp share links and an encrypted offsite copy. This page explains what runs where and what survives each kind of failure.
whatsapp_text: Hi, I'd like to understand how the hybrid AuraPACS setup would work at our centre.
persona: Centre owner or IT consultant comparing cloud, on-premise and hybrid PACS before choosing

paras: Hybrid PACS means the archive and viewer live on a machine in your building, and a cloud service mirrors what is needed for people outside the building. In AuraPACS the node handles DICOM receive, the modality worklist, the local archive, the browser viewer and reporting. The cloud layer handles remote viewing from home or a second site, the secure links you send on WhatsApp, and the encrypted offsite backup.

The split is deliberate. Indian centres deal with power cuts, shared fibre lines and afternoons when the uplink crawls. Pure cloud fails on the day the line is down. Pure on-premise fails on the day a disk dies or the radiologist is out of town. Hybrid is the arrangement where neither failure stops the centre.

sections.eyebrow: The two ways single-location PACS fails
sections.h2: Cloud-only and on-premise-only each have one bad day a month.
sections.lead: Neither model is wrong. Each just has a failure it cannot absorb, and small centres cannot afford a spare of everything.

items.p: Studies queue on the scanner, the viewer will not load, the reporting backlog grows until the connection returns.
A cloud viewer streaming a multi-series MR over a congested line makes the radiologist wait for every slice.
An on-premise server with no offsite copy loses years of studies to one hardware fault.
On-premise-only means reading happens inside the building or through a VPN someone has to maintain.
Without a cloud endpoint, sharing a study means a CD or a printed film again.

items.h: Power cut in the middle of a scan
items.p: Any PACS goes dark without power, but what matters is how quickly the node is back and whether anything was lost.

sections.h2: The node and the cloud layer, task by task.

steps.p: Modalities send DICOM to the node on the local network. No internet involved.
Scheduled patients are pushed to the machine so nothing is retyped.
Studies are indexed locally and opened in a browser from any PC on the network.
Templates, sign-off and the PDF are all done against the local copy.
When online, an encrypted copy of each study syncs offsite.
Radiologists read from outside, and WhatsApp links resolve, through the cloud layer.

sections.h2: Where the PACS lives, three ways.
rows: Local reads continue if installed on site
Local reads, reports and worklist continue

items.q: Is hybrid two products or one?
items.a: One. AuraPACS installs as a node on your network and the cloud layer is part of the same system. You do not buy an on-premise licence and then a cloud subscription from someone else.

items.q: What exactly stops when the internet drops?
items.a: Remote reading from outside the centre, WhatsApp share links and the offsite sync. Receiving studies, the worklist, local viewing and reporting all continue on the node. See on-premise PACS for the node in detail.

items.q: How does the offsite copy work?
items.a: Each study on the node is copied, encrypted, to the cloud layer when the connection is available. If the node's disk fails, the archive is restored from that copy.

items.q: Can a radiologist read from home?
items.a: Yes. Authorised users open synced studies in a browser from anywhere, with role-based access and every view audited. See remote reading.

items.q: Do we need to manage the cloud ourselves?
items.a: No. The cloud layer is operated as part of AuraPACS. Your IT person installs the node with remote guidance and points the modalities at it; the rest is configured for you.

items.q: Is the hybrid setup slower than pure on-premise?
items.a: Local reading is the same, because the viewer serves from the node. The sync to the cloud runs in the background and does not sit between the scanner and the reading screen.
